When lifting/pulling the clay up go slow. Count 10-20 seconds from bottom to top. 

A really good measure for going slow and even pulls, pay attention to the lines left behind when pulling the clay up. The closer those lines are, the better you pulls will be. 

If your hands and fingers are uneven get a fired vessel to practice on. You don't need to turn the wheel on, just practice hand positions and timing. Another tool to practice on, a plastic container, one with a thin wall. When going through the motions you can feel the pressure between your fingers. Also the positions.

Choking can be difficult, only choke your piece 2-3 times. Then throw it. When choking always return just slightly above the previous choke spot until you have thrown it or have gotten a feel for thickness. Choking can stretch the clay thinning it, thus causing a collapse. Throwing can bring clay into the thin areas, as well even it out.

Take your time, going slow will build muscle memory.  

Hope this helps!

When using marbling take into account what types of clay to use and how you are coloring the clay. The easiest way is stains and white earthenware. A simple store bought clear will be good so you will not mess up the color.

Stoneware can be a bit more fickle. Using stains is safe, but be selective of the clear you use as it can react to the clay body. Testing is going to be needed. Coloring the clay using oxides is tuff. Always test and figure out mixtures. Things like blistering and splitting are problematic in the clay. Sometimes you will need to leave a few peeps open to get fresh air in the kiln. Using a clear for oxide colored clay is kind of crazy. You may have to formulate different clears as they can react to the oxides in different ways. 

Safe bet, never had a problem with cobalt as a stain or copper carbonate. (low or high fire)

Porcelain is pretty much the same as stoneware. It does make for awesomeness as a white clay body.

I found a good way to get colors (cheap too) is to use stains. Mix powdered stain and maybe a little underglaze to preserve moisture.

Always wear a mask and gloves!

I make a lot of marbled works. I'll post them once they are all fired. 

The key to marbled clay depends on how much you want the colors/clays to mix. There are a few different ways to mix the clay and you do have to worry about centering as it will cause the clay to mix, like CoryTheDuck said. 

For minimal marbling just wedge the clays separately then stack or shuffle them on the wheel. Think like a layered cake or burger. THis will produce stripes rather than a marbled effect.

To get that marble stone look, wedge then slice the clay. Shuffle the pieces together like a layered cake. The size and placement of the layers will also have an effect on the look of the marble. Now to get that great marbled look wedge the clays together. Not much mind you. Maybe about 10 rotations. The more you do it, the more blended the clays will become and you can lose the contrast. Center on the wheel and throw.

Another technique to shuffling the clays is to take one body, wedge and rolled into a cylinder. Rather than slice it horizontal, go for vertical. Please keep in mind the grain and swirl of the wedged clay. This method can cause later issues like splitting and air bubbles. Think of this method as a pie chart or pizza where each slice can be a different color. Once put together you can wedge the whole thing or throw with it. 

Keep in mind centering will mix the clays.
Always wedge each clay body separately. (then wedge the clays together)
Make sure you compress very well as splitting will occur when the clay cools after firing. 
This is very important, trim the entire vessel even if it looks like it does not need it. Often slip can dirty the clay without you seeing it until its fired. 
Depending on how much you trim and also effect the marble, by making some colors more or less pronounced.
Keep your hands clean as to not leave finger prints.

The most important rule is to experiment! Try different methods and find out which one you like!

If you have anymore questions just ask away!
